subject: Onboarding: Performance & Cost Tuning blueprint for GreenGrid Analytics
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Onboarding: Performance & Cost Tuning blueprint for GreenGrid Analytics

Hi Priya / Alex —

Great to get the pilot signed. To make the first 30 days high-impact, I sketched a short, focused onboarding blueprint that ties the implementation work to measurable cost & latency outcomes. The goal: a working integration + one round of cost/perf tuning so you leave the pilot with a predictable ops profile and recommended quantization/routing settings.

High-level plan (week 0-4):
- Week 0: Implementation handoff + ingest profile review (we'll look at sample calls you attached)
- Week 1: Baseline perf run (1M tokens equivalent) to gather batching and KV-cache hit statistics
- Week 2: Iterative tuning experiments (batching, KV prefetch, two quant profiles)
- Week 3: Canary rollout with routing policy (primary low-latency variant + cheaper fallback)
- Week 4: Handoff docs, cost projection, and next-step proposal

Initial asks from your side: sample traffic trace (CSV) + representative prompt sets (3–5). I see you uploaded greengrid_map_of_calls.csv to the Drive — thanks. Can you also include one mid-size prompt that is latency-sensitive and one bulk batch workload?

I attached a lightweight mutual action plan (GG-mutual-action-plan-v2.docx) and a quick prefetch profile preview (prefetch_profile_preview.json) to show how we'd model KV-cache prewarm. We'll propose concrete batch sizes and target SLOs after the baseline run.

Proposed call: Monday 06/03 10:00am PT to align owners and schedule the baseline run. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Thanks for scheduling — quick notes for the call so we stay practical:

Call agenda (30m):
1) Owners + success criteria (who owns baseline runs, who signs off on cost plan)
2) Walk through the sample traces and identify two representative profiles (interactive, batch)
3) Proposed measurement plan: live baseline (no caching, default quant), then 3 experiments:
   - Exp A: batching sweep (batch sizes 1, 4, 8) measuring p50/p95 and token cost
   - Exp B: KV prefetch (warm top-100 prefixes) measuring cache hit rate and latency delta
   - Exp C: quant profile comparison (FP16 / int8 / nf4) measuring quality delta (BLEU-like surrogate) and cost
4) Canary routing strategy: route 90% traffic to primary variant (low-latency int8/optimized kernels) and 10% to baseline for quality guardrails
5) Next steps & MOA deliverables (docs and cost estimates)

I'll own the measurement plan with Sean as implementation lead. Mina — can you capture decisions in the mutual action plan? Priya/Alex — we'll need a short quality rubric for the quant experiments (2–3 test prompts you'd consider gating).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@greengrid.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Performance & Cost Tuning blueprint for GreenGrid Analytics

On implementation details — a few concrete items I want to call out before the baseline run:

1) Baseline environment: we'll spin up a dedicated test pool with same CPU/GPU family as production (A100-80GB equivalent) and pin the sequence length to your 1k median. Please confirm median sequence length from the trace.

2) Batching: we'll instrument continuous batching with target latency ceiling 250ms for p50 during interactive experiments. Expect optimal batch sizes in the 2–6 range given your trace (we'll sweep).

3) KV-cache prefetch: we'll run a small prewarm job that primes the top-500 KV prefixes for the common prompts. That should push cache-hit from ~5% to ~65% for interactive flows if your prompts are stable. Note: prefetch increases memory usage; we'll show memory footprint in the report.

4) Quant profiles: we'll test (a) FP16 baseline, (b) int8 dynamic, (c) nf4.optim — nf4.optim tends to give the best cost/quality trade for instruction-tuned models in our catalog. We'll capture a quality delta metric using your rubric.

5) Routing policies: our recommended canary is time-based (first 48 hours) + traffic split. If latency regressions appear, automated fallback to baseline is immediate. We'll include a rollback playbook.

I'll bring a simple runbook and an instrumentation dashboard for the call.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
